sentences.text: *J U D G M E N T*

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of M.V. Act, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.
Subhash.C

vs Nandini on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76303830/
1

*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL*
2. Facts leading to the case of the petitioner forthcoming in the petition that, on 24.5.2022 at about 8.00 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-41-EH-1244 on Railway Parallel Road, near D.Suhasini Hospital, Kengeri, Bengaluru City, at that time, driver of the car bearing registration No.GA-05-B-7938 suddenly opened the door, without any indication and negligent manner.
Due to the impact, the petitioner was fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3. It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to Adarsha Hospital, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
The petitioner had spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment.
4. It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 26 years, working in a private company and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
And he used to spend the said amount, for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to his severe injuries.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the car bearing No.GA-05-B-7938.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Kengeri Traffic Police as per Crime No.162/2022 under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
As such, the respondent No.1, being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
6. After registration of the case, as usual notices were issued to the respondents.
In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court, remained absent, placed exparte.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement, in answer to the case of the petitioner.
7. In the written statement of the respondent No.2, has not seriously disputed the accident, and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
But, strongly denied the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further stated that, the respondent No.2 has issued policy in respect of vehicle bearing registration No.GA-05-B-7938 and it was valid as on the date of accident.

It is the main contention of the respondent that, the accident had occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the petitioner, who was riding his motor cycle bearing NO.KA-41-EH- 1244 in a rash and negligent manner without D.L. and without wearing helmet.
It is the contention of the respondent that, the driver had no valid and effective driving license to drive the said vehicle.
Ultimately stated that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner, is highly excessive, exorbitant and without any basis.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.
8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, for final determination of the case, following issues are framed;
* ISSUES

* 
Subhash.C vs Nandini on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76303830/

2 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident,
that was taken place on 24.5.2022 at about 8.00 p.m. on Railway Parallel road, near D.Suhasini Hospital, Kengeri, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing registration No.GA-05-B-7938 in an actionable negligence ?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate ? from whom?
3) What order or award?

9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner by name Subhash C. during the course of evidence placed his affidavit evidence, in lieu of examination-in-chief, who examined as PW1 in the case on hand.
At the time of his evidence, 19 documentary evidence got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P19.
Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of Medical Record Officer of Adarsha Hospital by name Ashok N.S. as PW2.
At the time of his evidence placed 5 documents as per Ex.P20 to Ex.P24.
In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Naren as PW3.
At the time of his evidence, 2 documentary evidence, got marked as Ex.P25 & Ex.P26, for consideration.
10. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not led any rebuttal evidence for consideration, to prove all the defenses forthcoming in the written statement against the case of the petitioner.
11. Heard the arguments of both the counsel.
Perused the materials available on record.

At the time of the argument, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has relied on the authority reported in,
I.L.R 2012 KAR Page No. 4983 between Chandrashekar V/S. Sri. Revanasiddappa Danadamani and Another.

sentences.text: 12. With due respect, I have gone through the proposition laid down in the aforesaid case, on the point of appreciation of the evidence of the doctor.
It was observed that, the Tribunal should be more careful, while assessing the medical evidence.
The Tribunals may not accept such evidence at its face value.

On appreciation of the evidence available on record, my findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
*R E A S O N S* ISSUE NO.1:-
13.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, Car bearing registration No.GA-05-B-7938 alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Subhash.C vs Nandini on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76303830/
3 14.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle, remained absent and placed exparte, without challenging the case of the petitioner.

The respondent No.2 being the insurance company, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, strongly denied the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, by contending that, due to the sole negligence on the part of the petitioner, alleged accident and its consequences were taken place.
Further, to prove all the defenses put forth in the written statement of the respondent company, has not adduced any rebuttal evidence for consideration.
In such a situation, duty is more on the part of the court to assess the available evidence on record, in order to come to the proper conclusion in connection with the above issue.

15. On taking birds eye view towards the pleadings of the petitioner, along with the above issue, It is crystal clear that, as per section 101 of Evidence Act, and under section 166 of M.V. Act, burden is on the petitioner, to prove the same, on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
The petitioner-Subhash C., to discharge the burden lies on him, relied on his affidavit evidence in lieu of examination-in-chief and examined as PW1.
In his affidavit reiterated all the averments made in the main petition.
In support of the injuries sustained by him, relied on the evidence of PW2 and PW3 along with the medical documents.
Among the documentary evidence, Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12 as well as Ex.P.21 and Ex.P.22 are the material documents in connection with the above issue.

Remaining documents and the evidence of the PW2 and PW3 are to be discussed in detail, at the time of discussion on issue No.2.
16.
On taking birds eye view towards the documents relied on by the petitioner, in connection with this issue, go to show that, alleged accident had taken place, on 24.05.2022.
First information in this regard was given on 28.05.2022 by one B. Chandrashekar.
The complainant is none other than the father of the petitioner.

In connection with the point of delay in giving first information is concerned, the complainant had stated in his complaint and also it is forthcoming in the Ex.P.1 column No.3(c) that, the owner of the car, at the first instance agreed to bear the expenses of the treatment, subsequently, he has not kept his word.
Hence, belated complaint has been given.
To disprove the reasons mentioned in the complaint, as well as in the Ex.P.1, no contra materials available on record, from the side of the respondents.
In connection with the above facts and circumstances of the case, no suspected circumstances emerging to disbelieve the reason for delay.
Hence, the point of four days delay in giving first information by the father of the petitioner is not fatal in the case on hand.
When the petitioner had sustained grevious injuries in the accident, one cannot expect, immediate complaint from his father.

17. On the basis of the first information given by the first informant, criminal law set in motion against the driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.GA-05-B-7938 alleging that, the driver had committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
In the recitals of the complaint, marked at Ex.P2, there is a clear narration with respect to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle in question.

To disprove all the allegations forthcoming in para No.10 of Ex.P1 and in the recitals of Ex.P2, the driver of the offending vehicle car, or its owner have not made an effort to question the same, well in time before the competent court of law.

As such, the material documents in the case on hand, which laid down the foundation against the alleged negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, remained Subhash.C vs Nandini on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76303830/
4 unquestioned.
Added to this, the statement of the injured, and an eye witnesses, marked at Ex.P.3 to Ex.P.5 are also, supports the Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 to be believed.

18. Added to this, the spot mahazar Ex.P.6, relied on by the petitioner, goes to show that, after setting criminal law in motion against the driver of the offending vehicle, the investigation officer,
visited the scene of occurrence and conducted the mahazar process in the presence of punch witness, the said document, reveals about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
Apart from this, the investigation officer at the time of mahazar had drawn spot sketch as per Ex.P.7.

There is no explanation from the respondents, how the offending vehicle found in the place of accident, if at the said vehicle was not responsible for the accident, why the driver of the offending vehicle or its owner have not gave counter complaint against the petitioner, if at all there is negligence on the part of the petitioner.

19. Added to this, police notice and reply to the police notice, report of the motor vehicle inspector,
and wound certificate marked at Ex.P.8 to Ex.P.11 reveal that, the owner of the offending vehicle has not disputed the involvement of his vehicle in the accident, in his reply to the police notice.

Further,
the alleged accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles involved in the accident in question.
The damages noted in the report of the IMV inspector remained unquestioned.

If at all the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident, at the time of seizure and inspecting the vehicle,
why the owner of the said vehicle, not questioned the same, to prove the point of innocence of his driver.
Another document wound certificate goes to show that, on the history of RTA, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
All these material documents remained unquestioned.

20. Ultimately, on perusal of the final report Ex.P.12, submitted by the investigation officer against Srinath, alleging that, he had committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC,
substantiates the case of the petitioner.
Though the police papers are not substantive piece of evidence to consider the claim petition, in the absence of contra materials, no hurdle to believe the recitals of the said documents.

The respondent company herein, except filing written statements,
not made an effort to place contra materials, to impeach the police papers and the evidence of the petitioner.
Apart from this, the MLC extract and Police intimation marked at Ex.P.21 and Ex.P.22 also supports the case of the petitioner herein.

21. Another point to be noted herein that, even at the time of cross examination of the PW1, though several questions and suggestions put to the witness, in para No. 2 to 5, at page No.7 and 8, on appreciation of the answers given by the PW1, in toto, along with the recitals of the police documents and in the absence of the rebuttal evidence from the side of the respondents makes this court to come to the conclusion that, nothing has been elicited to disbelieve the case of the petitioner, and to prove the innocence of the driver of the offending vehicle, as well as to the allegations made against the petitioner in the case on hand.
22.

Over all appreciation of entire evidence of the petitioner, I am of the view that, the petitioner herein, has placed convincing and cogent evidence in connection with the above issue, by way of affidavit and the documentary evidence, which speak that, the alleged accident was occurred, due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, bearing registration Subhash.C vs Nandini on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76303830/
5 No.GA-05-B-7938.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the Issue No.1, is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
23.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident, under different heads.

24. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another.

entities.text: Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.

"
25. In connection with the injuries sustained by the petitioner, in the accident, had produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P11.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Avulsion Crush injury with Avulsion of EDL and peroneal tendons--left lower limb 2) Progressive muscle necrosis and infarction of anterolateral compartment of Leg 26.
As per the pinion of the doctor, the aforesaid injuries are grievous in nature.
Further the petitioner has produced discharge summary, photographs, CD, medical bills, prescriptions as per Ex.P13 to Ex.P17.
Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of Medical Record Officer by name Ashok N.S. as PW2.
He has placed MLC extract, police intimation, entire case sheet and x-ray along with authorization as per Ex.P20 to Ex.P24.
In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Naren as PW3.

At the time of his evidence placed outpatient record and x-ray as per Ex.P25 &
Ex.P26.
By taking into consideration of the nature of the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment.

On going through the discharge summary of Adarsh Hospital, marked at Ex.P13 goes to show that the petitioner had taken Subhash.C vs Nandini on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76303830/
6 treatment from 24.5.2022 to 13.6.2022.

entities.text: Subhash.C vs Nandini on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For having taken note of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, it is apt to consider the compensation of Rs.70,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.
27. Another point to be discussed herein, about the loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
In the petition, he had stated that, he was working as a consultant/real estate agent and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, to substantiate the same, there is no iota of documents to show the income of the petitioner as Rs.25,000/- per month, as on the date of the accident.
On going through the discharge summary of Adarsh Hospital, marked at Ex.P13 goes to show that the petitioner has taken treatment from 24.5.2022 to 13.6.2022.

On the other hand,
during period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to him, to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for two months.
Hence, I am of the view that, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.31,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

28. The petitioner herein, in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence,
placed 72 medical bills of Rs.3,76,086/- as per Ex.P16 along with prescriptions as per Ex.P17.
On going through the said medical bills, Sl.No.1 to Sl.No.48 of Ex.P16 are medicine bills in toto of Rs.3,10,664.19.
On the other hand, Sl.No.49 to Sl.No.72 are physiotherapy in toto of Rs.63,025/-.

In connection with the physitherapy bills, on going through the medica bills submitted by the petitioner and also admission from the side of PW1, at the time of cross-examination at page No.10 along with the answers given by the PW3, at the time of his cross-examination, at page No.5 in para No.3, there is no specific advise from the doctor to the petitioner to undergo physiotherapy.
On going through the physiotherapy bills, reveals that, in the year 2022 to 2023, the petitioner had undergone physiotherapy.
But to substantiate the said bills, not made an effort to examine the author of the said bills issued as per Sl.No.49 to Sl.No.72, nor placed the evidence of the doctor in this regard.

Hence, on appreciation of entire medical bills, I am of the view that, it is apt to grant only Rs.25,000/- to the petitioner in connection with the expenses of physiotherapy along with medical bills of Sl.No.1 to Sl.No.48 in toto of Rs.3,10,664.19.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,10,664/-, under the head of medical expenses.

29. The petitioner herein, as per the medical records, especially, the wound certificate and also on going through the evidence of PW1, and document placed by him, reflects that, the petitioner had sustained avulsion crush injury with avulsion of EDL and Peroneal tendons left lower limb.
On going through the discharge summary of Adarsh Hospital, marked at Ex.P13 goes to show that the petitioner has taken treatment from 24.5.2022 to 13.6.2022.

Hence, during the period of treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food,
nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards attendant charges, food, and nourishment and conveyance charges.
30. Another material point of loss of future income is concerned, the petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.

In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate,
with other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1, reiterated the same thing forthcoming in Subhash.C vs Nandini on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76303830/
7 the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him, as per Ex.P11, goes to show that, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed, wound certificate and x-ray for consideration.
Apart from this, the petitioner had placed the evidence of the doctor by name Dr.Naren as PW3.

In addition to this, PW2 Medical Record Officer has placed MLC extract, police intimation, entire case and x-ray as per Ex.P21 to Ex.P24.
31.
In the evidence of this material witness PW3, deposed that, consequent upon the accident the petitioner had sustained avulsion crush injury with avulsion of EDL and peronial tendons left lower limb.
In this regard, he underwent surgeries of wound debridement and tendon repair under spinal anesthesia on 25.5.2022.
Wound debridement and VSE dressing under spinal anesthesia on 28.5.2022, skin grafting of raw area under spinal anesthesia on 9.6.2022.
At the time of his discharge on 13.6.2022 he was advised to follow-up treatment on OPD basis.

32. At the time of examination of this witness on 23.9.2023, in order to assess the disability on the basis of clinical radiological examination as well as by virtue of complaints of the petitioner, found vital stable, wounds scar of SSG over left leg and dorsum of foot, reduced sensation over SSG scar and distal foot dorsum, scar induration present, ankles stiffness present, foot and toe dorsiflexion and eversion weak, gait is having slight limp, scar over right thigh SSG donor site.
X-ray shown left foot and ankle normal, left knee and hip normal.

Further he deposed that, on the basis of disability on the point of mobility components, stability components along with extra points and in the shelter of Gazette Notification, witness, came to the conclusion that, mobility + stability disability at 21.33%.
Limb physical impairment 30.33% and whole body disability impairment is at 10%.
Apart from this, he opined that, the petitioner has been advised for scar reduction surgery using tissue expander cost of which is about Rs.3,00,000/-.

In support of the evidence of the PW3 placed outpatient record and x- ray as per Ex.P25 & Ex.P26.
33.
At the time of cross-examination of this witness, admitted that, he is not the treated doctor.

As per the wound certificate, and discharge surgery he came to know about the mode of treatment taken by the petitioner, at the time of discharge from the hospital, his physical condition was satisfactory.

In connection with the advise of physiotherapy, no specific mention in the medical documents of the petitioner, as well as he has not seen the following medical documents, for having advised about the physiotherapy.
Further, he answered that, the petitioner had undergone 3 plastic surgeries, but no any fracture injuries.
Further, he admitted that, he ha snot taken MRI report of the petitioner, he came to know about the physiotherapy, only on the basis of oral statement of the petitioner.

Further, he admitted that, there was no injury in connection with the joint of the petitioner, but denied the suggestion that, there is no reduction of muscle strength of the petitioner and in continuation he stated that he shown in his report as 4%.

Further, he denied the suggestion that, he assessed the percentage of disability in connection with mobility and stability components in higher side, and answered that, the pain pertaining to the petitioner is permanent in nature, but there is no any restriction in connection with the movement of the petitioner.

Further, he answered that, in connection with the nerve damage of the petitioner ha snot taken any opinion from neurologist or orthopedic surgeon, he admitted that he has not produced x-ray report, he expressed only in connection with the physical disability of the petitioner.

Further, he admitted that, in connection with the future treatment, there is no whisper in the medical documents of the Subhash.C vs Nandini on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76303830/
8 petitioner, and he has not placed any quotation in connection with the future medical expenses of the petitioner.
Ultimately, he denied the suggestion that, he assessed the disability of the petitioner in connection with whole body is in higher side.

34. Over all appreciation of entire medical documents of the petitioner along with the evidence of PW3, I am of the view that, percentage of disability in connection with whole body pertaining to the petitioner expressed by the PW3, seems just to be accepted.
Hence, it is apt to take wholebody disability of the petitioner as 10%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
35. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 26 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed Aadhar card and driving licence marked at Ex.P18 & Ex.P19, for consideration.
On going through the said documents pertaining to the petitioner, the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 2.10.1996.
The accident occurred on 24.5.2022.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 26 years.

To the said age as per Sarla Verma case,
multiplier '17' is to be taken into consideration.

36. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in the main petition, and also in the examination-in-chief evidence, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, prior to the accident, he was working as a consultant/real estate agent and getting an income of Rs.25,000/- per month.
In support of his avocation, and definite income per month, he has not placed any iota of documents.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But, the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.

Hence, by keeping in mind about the year of the institution of this case, and also, as per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/- for the year 2022.
37. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner

,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,500X 12 X 17 X10/100= Rs.3,16,200/-.
38.

Next factual aspect loss of amenities is concerned, due to the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate and in other medical documents, and on appreciation of the evidence of the PW3, in toto,
I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work,
as well as his work for livelihood.
By taking into consideration of all these aspects, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities.

39. In connection with the future medication expenses is concerned, PW3 has stated that, the petitioner has advised scar reduction surgery using tissue expander, the cost of the said surgery is about Rs.3,00,000/-.
To substantiate this, no estimation placed for consideration.

As such, by looking in to the entire facts and circumstances of the case, and also by looking in to the advice of Subhash.C vs Nandini on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76303830/
9 the treated doctor at the time of the discharge, and in the absence of the follow-up documents, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of future medical expenses.

40. In view of my due discussions held above, on various aspects, the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 70,000-00 2.Loss of income during laid- Rs. 31,000-00 up period and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs.3,10,664-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 20,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5.Loss of future income due Rs.3,16,200-00 to disability 6.
Loss of Amenities Rs. 30,000-00 7.
Future medication Rs. 30,000-00 Total Rs.8,07,864-00 41.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,07,864/- (Rupees eight lakhs seven thousand eight hundred and sixty four only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

LIABILITY:
42.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.GA-05-B-7938 alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

As such, it is the strong assertion of the petitioner that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
43. As per the records insurance policy was valid from 3.5.2022 to 2.5.2023.
The alleged accident had taken place on 24.5.2022.
This aspect and existence of insurance policy has not been seriously disputed by the other side.
There is no evidence about the violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

44. As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay Subhash.C vs Nandini on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76303830/
10 compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2, being the insurance company and indemnifier has to satisfy the award.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
